message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties**

| Property | Value / Description | Notes |
|----------|---------------------|-------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 | Only one proton in the nucleus. |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.00794 u (average) | Dominated by the most abundant isotope, ^1H. |
| **Isotopes** | ^1H (protium, 99.98 %), ^2H (deuterium, 0.02 %), ^3H (tritium, trace, radioactive). | Deuterium and tritium are used in nuclear fusion research. |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ | One valence electron → highly reactive. |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 | Highest among all elements. |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) | Highest of all elements. |
| **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV (–72.8 kJ mol⁻¹) | Negative value indicates energy release when H gains an electron. |
| **Molecular form** | H₂ (diatomic) | Stable under normal conditions; forms covalent bonds. |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) | Extremely low; requires cryogenic temperatures. |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) | Liquid hydrogen exists only at very low temperatures. |
| **Density (at 0 °C, 1 atm)** | 0.08988 g cm⁻³ | Less dense than air; rises to the ceiling. |
| **Specific heat (gas, 25 °C)** | 14.304 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹ | High due to light mass. |
| **Molar volume (ideal gas, 0 °C, 1 atm)** | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ | Standard reference. |
| **Reactivity** | Extremely reactive; forms hydrides with metals, acids, and many nonmetals. | Forms H₂O, H₂S, HF, etc. |
| **Bonding** | Forms single covalent bonds; can form H–H, H–O, H–C, H–N, etc. | Can also form ionic bonds as H⁺ (proton) or H⁻ (hydride). |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman, Balmer, Paschen series (UV, visible, IR) | Classic hydrogen emission spectrum. |
| **Role in biology** | Essential for water, organic molecules, energy carriers (ATP). | Hydrogen bonds stabilize DNA, proteins. |
| **Industrial uses** | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells), ammonia synthesis (Haber–Bosch), petroleum refining, metal processing. | Clean energy potential. |
| **Safety** | Highly flammable; forms explosive mixtures with air (1–4 % H₂ in air). | Requires careful handling. |
| **Environmental impact** | When combusted, produces only water vapor; no CO₂. | Potentially green fuel if produced from renewables. |

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element** – only one proton and one electron.
- **Highly reactive** – strongest electronegativity, high ionization energy.
- **Diatomic gas** – H₂ is the most common form at ambient conditions.
- **Extremely low boiling/melting points** – requires cryogenic temperatures to liquefy.
- **Key in energy & chemistry** – fuels, fertilizers, hydrogen bonding in biology.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property!
